name: Learn with Kody
about: Walkthroughs for the Vibe Coding Examples. Every episode takes one example end to end: the exact seed prompt, what the agent actually returned, the measurement that caught what was wrong, and the fix. Follow along, pause anywhere, run it yourself.
_hosting: This channel lives inside the kody-w.github.io repo. GitHub Pages serves every repo of a user from one origin, so it plays in the RAPP Vision player at /rapp-vision while being published, versioned and owned right here next to the examples it documents.

videos.title: An open-world city in one HTML file — and a gate that failed for the wrong reason
videos.description: Episode 3. A drivable procedural coastal city as ONE self-contained HTML file: no npm, no Vite, no build step, and not a single image file — every texture is drawn into a canvas at runtime, because with no asset pipeline there is nowhere else to put one. The whole world builds in 51.5ms. Then an independent acceptance gate re-measured every claim the builder made instead of trusting its self-report. It came back 10/11, failing on the most important check: is the simulation paced by the wall clock or by the frame rate? The app was fine. The gate had probed for a clock at a name the app does not use. That was the seventh time in one session that a reported failure turned out to be the test rather than the code. Corrected, it passes: day-fraction advance of 1.851e-3/s unthrottled versus 1.856e-3/s under 8x CPU throttle, a ratio of 1.002. The best line in the builder's own report was a caveat — CPU throttling had barely moved its frame rate, so rather than publish the clean number it proved the throttle was genuinely applied (a JS benchmark went 2.7ms to 56ms) and explained why, then re-ran the test with a main-thread hog that collapsed the frame rate 8.95x and got the same answer.

videos.title: Six times the test was wrong: a buzzsaw pass over one 9,749-line file
videos.description: Episode 2. Eight agents on one self-contained HTML file: six builders owning disjoint regions, two read-only critics whose only job was to be unimpressed. They found 21 real defects, including a blocker already in git HEAD where every button in the desktop toolbar hit-tested to the Click-to-play overlay: clicking the gear granted pointer lock instead of opening Settings, and three panels had no keyboard fallback at all. It is invisible in the source and invisible in a screenshot. They also proved the day/night clock advanced by the clamped physics step, so the world ran at 36-66% of real time while every instrument built on that same clock agreed everything was fine. Now 96-105%. But the best finding is not a bug: the ambient occlusion was real, correct, wired up, and completely invisible, because roughly 1.9 irradiance with no tone mapping clips the very highlight it was meant to darken. The builder measured the attribute and never measured the pixel. And six times the reported failure was the test being wrong, not the code.

videos.title: Follow along: build a Gran Turismo-grade racing sim in one HTML file
videos.description: Episode 1. We build the Apex Driving Simulator from the exact seed prompt on the examples page, then do the part everyone skips: prove it. The agent reported success. A fan of dark streaks on the pit apron looked like broken skid marks, so it cleared the skid buffer, and the fan stayed. That is the moment to stop looking and start measuring. Walking all 1600 centreline points found a 7.28-degree heading change against a 0.378-degree median, all six worst values sitting together at the loop-closure seam. One discontinuity, three unrelated-looking bugs. Fixed by arc-length resampling with centred finite-difference tangents: 7.28 degrees down to 2.12, segments even at 0.650 m, barrier penetration 0.0000 m.

videos.title: LIVE: drive the finished sim yourself - no video file
videos.description: The same simulator, as a live replay instead of a recording. There is no video here. The player loads the real application and replays a recorded script on a clock, so you can pause at any point and take the wheel. A few KB of JSON doing the job of 26 MB of video. This is Tier 2 of rapp-remix: what the app does now, not what it did once.
videos._note: Addressed by id, not label: #btnCam renames itself Chase/Cockpit/Hood as it cycles. Action times are measured from the moment #startBtn becomes clickable, not from scene start, so the same script drives the same lap on a fast laptop or a slow phone. The throttle burst is short on purpose: this sim integrates physics per frame, and an identical longer pull reached 11.7 m/s on one run and 24.7 on the next.
